title: Evaluate retrieval before polishing answers
outcome: Build a query–evidence dataset and diagnose ingestion, retrieval, ranking, or generation failures.
cue: Measure whether the right evidence arrived before judging the prose.
version: Provider-neutral principles · Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 lab · legacy Ruby 2.7 adaptation notes
useCase: Build a query–evidence dataset and diagnose ingestion, retrieval, ranking, or generation failures.
benefits: A clear decision and a way to check it.
drawbacks: An impressive answer can conceal retrieval failure. Changing every pipeline component at once prevents a useful diagnosis.

trace.title: Label queries and supporting spans
trace.detail:
Create realistic questions with expected supporting documents/spans and answerability labels. Include paraphrases, exact terms, exceptions, stale documents, forbidden documents, ambiguity, and no-answer cases. Freeze a held-out set before tuning.

Recall@k asks whether expected relevant evidence is among the first k results under a defined relevance label. Precision@k asks how much of the retrieved set is relevant. Ranking metrics measure order. These are not final-answer accuracy, and relevance labels may have multiple valid supporting sources.

Check the pipeline in order: parsed source quality, candidate recall, ranking/context packing, answer support, access boundaries, latency and cost. Use an exact/scoped or lexical baseline. Keep permission leakage as a separate hard failure, not a small penalty hidden by an average relevance score.

trace.title: Follow one input
trace.detail: Choose fixtures → freeze expected evidence/answerability → run retrieval → compare stage IDs → inspect failure cases → tune one component → rerun on holdout. Keep document/index versions in the experiment.

trace.detail: An impressive answer can conceal retrieval failure. Changing every pipeline component at once prevents a useful diagnosis.
